```{r}
#| label: footer-options

options(housepi.footer.warranty = TRUE)
```

Some models support custom group rates.
A group rate multiplies one of the model's transmission rates, member by member, according to the member's group.
A group rate is *absolute*: each group gets its own rate, and the model's baseline rate is then fixed to `1`.
Choosing a reference group makes the rate *relative* instead: the baseline rate holds for the reference, and each parameter is the rate ratio of one group to that reference.
A rate ratio is not a risk ratio, because the probability of infection is $1 - e^{-\lambda}$ for a rate $\lambda$.
With a 30% probability of infection in the reference group, a rate ratio of 2 raises it to 51%, a risk ratio of 1.7.
Each such model declares the group rates it supports, and each of them can be redefined.
We provide an example here with the heterogeneous version of the case-ascertained model.

# Format data covariates

Suppose we want to explore age and sex effects within the household survey `sarscov2_2021_icofs` (see `?sarscov2_2021_icofs`).
We start by creating categorical groupings to stratify individuals based on their age, sex, etc. and then associate individual group rates.

```{r}
#| label: format-age-data
library(housepi)
set_housepi_theme(colour_strips = TRUE)
set_housepi_summary(cri_level = 0.95)
set.seed(42)

# define a model object
hh_model <- new_housepi_model(sarscov2_2021_icofs, "case-ascertained")
```

The loaded model supports several group rates, including the individual `"susceptibility"` (see the `$help()` method or `?template_case_ascertained`).
We can define it calling `add_group_rate()`.
A group rate without a definition is `1` for everyone. A definition adds a new parameter for each group, and one more for the reference group unless a reference is chosen.

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-by-age
hh_model |>
  # associate susceptibility group rate by column age
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", by = "age") |>
  # inspect group rate definitions
  get_group_rates()
```
To return a group rate to its default, overwrite its definition with argument `by` set to `NA`.
To drop all previous definitions, add a new one with `append = FALSE`.

# Dependencies between covariates

In the previous example we associated group rates to a single covariate in the data.
In this example we show how to provide more covariates and a reference, which makes the rate relative.
Manually set a `reference` by providing the corresponding group factor values, or ask for `".auto"` to take the largest group:

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-by-sex-age
hh_model |>
  # multiplicative group rates, adult female chosen as reference
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult")) |>
  # show corresponding tables with associations
  get_group_rates()
```

By default, the parameters of each grouping are independent,
i.e. the group rate is the product of two parameters, one for the covariate "sex", another for "age".
Alternatively, we can make the rate joint between the covariates:

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-joint
hh_model |>
  # here covariates are assumed to be joint
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult"),
                 joint = TRUE) |>
  get_group_rates()
```

# Parameters associated to rates

Inference needs a prior and a proposal for each group parameter.
By default, an absolute group rate assumes a uniform prior over its support, while a relative one assumes a lognormal prior (`meanlog = 0` and `sdlog = 3`), following @cauchemez_household_2009.
The group rate definition takes the same MCMC arguments as a parameter definition.

```{r}
#| label: group-rate-parameters
# default parameter associated to group rates
hh_model |>
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"), prefix = "") |>
  get_parameters()

# custom parameter priors associated to group rates
hh_model |>
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"), prefix = "",
                 prior = "normal") |>
  get_parameters()

```

# Inference with group rates

We can proceed with the inference as shown in [Get started](housepi.html):

```{r}
#| label: final-group-rates

hh_model <- hh_model |>
  # load group rates from definition list, both relative to keep beta free
  add_group_rate(
    infectivity = list(by = "isolated", reference = ".auto"),
    susceptibility = list(by = "vacc_status", reference = "unvaccinated")
  )

# show parameter definitions used for the inference
get_parameters(hh_model)
```


```{r}
#| label: inference-group-rates
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Six trace plots displaying MCMC sampling behaviour for model parameters: alpha, beta, infectivity by isolation, and susceptibility parameters stratified by vaccination status.
#|  Multiple chains (1-3) are overlaid across iterations, showing convergence diagnostics and mixing properties of the Markov chains.

hh_model <- hh_model |>
  # parameter definitions
  add_parameter(
    alpha = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "rw_log"),
    beta = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "rw_log"),
    gamma = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "rw_unif", max = 5),
    hh_size_ref = 4
  ) |>
  # latent definitions
  add_latent(
    # public definitions
    infec_time = list(min = end_date - 29, max = test_date + 1),
    # accessory definitions, generic to all statuses
    incub_period = list(model = "gamma", mean = 3, sd = 1.4)
  ) |>
  # observation model
  add_observation(
    #> symptomatic (status = 1)
    test_date = list(
      status = 1, model = "normal",
      mean = infec_time + incub_period, sd = 1, min = floor(infec_time)
    ),
    #> asymptomatic (status = 2)
    test_date = list(
      status = 2, model = "uniform",
      loc = floor(infec_time), min = 0, max = 8
    )
  ) |>
  # infectivity profile definitions
  add_infectivity_profile("gamma", mean = 4, sd = 1.6)

# perform inference
hh_fit <- hh_model |>
  run_inference(threads = 2, progress = 4)

bayesplot::mcmc_trace(get_parameter_draws(hh_fit))
```

# Compare group rates

The plot compares each susceptibility estimate with the reference group:

```{r}
#| label: compare-group-rates-plot
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Posterior estimates of relative susceptibility by vaccination status (1 dose, 2 doses, 3 doses), with unvaccinated as the reference.
#|  Points show median estimates with 95% credible intervals; bracketed labels give the number of individuals in each group.
library(ggplot2)

rate_id <- "susceptibility"

tmp <- get_group_rates(hh_model) |>
  # extract reference value and create a label
  dplyr::filter(group_rate == rate_id, param_name == ".reference") |>
  dplyr::select(vacc_status)
# an absolute rate has no reference row: the estimates read on their own
ylabel <- if (nrow(tmp) == 0) rate_id else
  sprintf("%s (ref: %s)", rate_id,
          paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = " "), collapse = " "))

# compare inferred susceptibility group rates
hh_fit |>
  summarise_draws() |>
  dplyr::filter(startsWith(variable, rate_id)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(get_group_rates(hh_model) |>
                     dplyr::select(param_name, n) |>
                     dplyr::rename(variable = param_name),
                   by = "variable") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    variable = gsub("_", " ", sub("susceptibility_vacc_status", "", variable))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = median, label = sprintf("[%s]", n))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "black") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(nudge_x = 0.2, nudge_y = 0.1, color = "coral") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q2.5, ymax = q97.5)) +
  labs(x = "", y = ylabel)
```
